display.purpose: The two direction titles on the console. Muted at rest, bone while live; weight 430 and width 134% while its voice speaks.

wordmark.purpose: The name on the empty page, in capitals; opens from width 25 / weight 900 to width 151 / weight 250.

section-title.purpose: Headings inside a dialog: a settings section, a service, a step of the setup guide.

caption.purpose: The translation of a sentence; scales with --caption-scale.

caption-source.purpose: The original of a sentence, in muted bone.

caption-urdu.purpose: Urdu translations in Nastaliq (line-height 2.1); Naskh by setting (line-height 1.75).

label.purpose: Names of things: speakers, languages, steps, services, measurement titles, field labels (10px, 0.16em) and tabs. Uppercase, 9px to 13px.

key-label.purpose: The lettering of the two keys; uppercase.

measurement.purpose: Figures over the console: last delay, sentences.

measurement-small.purpose: Clock times and delays in the conversation, slider values (11px), provider ids (10px), kbd (12px).

shadows.name: shadow-pop
shadows.purpose: The only shadow: dialogs, the services popover, menus, the jump-to-newest button.

shadows.name: focus-ring-field
shadows.purpose: Focused input, select and textarea, with a bone edge.

shadows.name: focus-ring-voice
shadows.purpose: The typing box while focused, in the chosen voice.

shadows.name: backdrop
shadows.purpose: Behind a dialog; arrives over 0.5s, leaves in 0.24s ease-in.

shadows.name: grain
shadows.value: feTurbulence fractalNoise 0.9, 2 octaves, 220px tile, opacity 0.085, fixed
shadows.purpose: Still grain over the dark ground; removed in Daylight.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.value: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)
motion.purpose: The default: quick to answer, long to settle, no overshoot.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.value: cubic-bezier(0.76, 0, 0.24, 1)
motion.purpose: Defined as a token for moves that start and end at rest.

motion.name: slow
motion.purpose: Sentences already present when the page opens coming into focus (opacity, blur 6px, rise 14px), newest first from 1.2s, 0.14s apart.

motion.name: entry-fade
motion.value: fade-in 0.7s ease-out; 0.3s delay on the first sentence after the empty page
motion.purpose: A live sentence appearing where it lands.

motion.name: entry-extras
motion.value: fade-in 0.9s ease-out +0.15s
motion.purpose: The other captions and the delay arriving beside the translation.

motion.name: button-sweep
motion.value: background-size 0.55s ease-out; color 0.3s +0.05s
motion.purpose: The fill of an outlined button.

motion.name: key-sweep
motion.value: background-size 0.7s ease-out; color 0.35s +0.06s
motion.purpose: A key's fill, from its own side.

motion.name: press
motion.value: scale 0.97 in 0.12s (icon buttons 0.92, send 0.96)
motion.purpose: Press feedback.

motion.name: signal
motion.value: 1.9s ease-out, once
motion.purpose: The line in the voice's colour over a translation that has just landed.

motion.name: reveal-lines
motion.value: GSAP SplitText lines + masks, yPercent 105 (Arabic script 160, masks opened by overflow-clip-margin 0.55em), 1.15s expo.out, stagger min(0.1, 0.32 / (lines - 1))
motion.purpose: A translation rising line by line.

motion.name: flow
motion.value: 1.5s linear infinite (pending line 1.6s)
motion.purpose: The light running along a line into the step at work.

motion.name: ping
motion.value: 1.6s ease-out infinite, scale 1 to 3.4, opacity 0.9 to 0
motion.purpose: The ring leaving a speaking lamp.

motion.name: title-speaking
motion.value: font-weight and font-stretch 1.1s, color 1.2s
motion.purpose: A direction title gaining weight while its voice speaks.

motion.name: tick
motion.value: 1s ease-out from clip-path inset(0 0 100% 0), translate 0 100%
motion.purpose: A measurement that changed rolls up like a counter wheel.

motion.name: step-back
motion.value: .entry__cell opacity 0.78 over 0.6s, .entry__lang to --text-muted; cleared 2.6s after the pointer rests
motion.purpose: Reading focus on one sentence or one language column; speaker, time and delay keep full strength.

motion.name: dialog-arrival
motion.value: opacity 0.45s, translate 22px and scale 0.985 over 0.6s; body fade-in 0.5s +0.08s
motion.purpose: Dialogs rise out of the dark; sheets arrive from 56px to the right.

motion.name: dialog-close
motion.value: opacity and translate (10px down; sheet 24px right) 0.24s ease-in, overlay and display allow-discrete; backdrop the same; content kept mounted 240ms
motion.purpose: Dialogs go back into the dark quicker than they came.

motion.name: tab-rule
motion.value: scale 0.5s ease-out from the left; color 0.3s
motion.purpose: The chosen tab's 1px rule.

motion.name: unfold
motion.value: 0.7s ease-out clip-path from the top (menus 0.6s)
motion.purpose: Popovers and menus.

motion.name: page-arrival
motion.value: GSAP timeline, expo.out, 1.6s default, opacity only; keys 0.9s at 0.05s; titles alone travel 30px with blur 10px over 2.2s at 0.3s; conversation at 1s; typing bar at 1.5s
motion.purpose: The page's opening, once.

motion.name: surface-arrival
motion.value: 3.2s, cubic ease-out, from the middle distance outwards
motion.purpose: The wave surface appearing.

motion.name: interlude-draft
motion.value: rules 2.2s at 0.6s; outline 2.8s power1.inOut at 1s; ink wipe 1.8s power2.inOut at 3.1s; outline rests at 0.3 from 4.4s; wordmark opacity 0.6s at 0.8s, width and weight 2.4s power2.inOut at 1.1s; copy lines 1.4s at 2s
motion.purpose: The empty page being drafted.

motion.name: interlude-exit
motion.value: opacity 0.3s power2.out, 12px lift 0.3s power1.in, no blur
motion.purpose: The empty page stepping away for the first sentence.

motion.name: reading-rest
motion.value: page turn 0.9s; settle onto a sentence start within 44px over 0.6s
motion.purpose: The conversation rests on whole sentences while a call is followed.

motion.name: smooth-scroll
motion.value: Lenis lerp 0.13, wheel only, on the GSAP ticker
motion.purpose: Inertia for the conversation.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: CSS durations 0.001ms; GSAP, Lenis and the simulation do not start
motion.purpose: Everything is still.

narrative.northStar: The Instrument in a Dark Room
narrative.overview:
Tarjuman is an instrument, not a page. A carbon ground under fine still grain carries bone-white linework and type, and the two voices of a call are drawn on it as light: ember for your own voice, warm like a lit filament, and frost for the other side, cold like daylight. Across the console lies one surface, a simulated sheet of water drawn as ridgelines at a low angle; each live voice drives its own end of it, and where the two waves meet in the middle the lines turn white. That meeting is the interpreting, and it is the one image the interface is built around.

Everything else serves reading during a live call. Structure is drawn with 1px hairlines as rules between things, the way a column is ruled, and the names of things are set in small, wide, spaced capitals like the lettering on a control desk. Captions are the largest text below the console and always the most legible. Motion is slow and exponential: things arrive out of the dark, fading in where they stand, nothing bounces, and with reduced motion everything is still. Dark is the design; "Daylight" is a light variant chosen in the settings, produced by the same tokens through `light-dark()`.

The system refuses both of its earlier selves: the neon "AI studio" of purple glows, gradient ribbons and glass, and the pale editorial page. The owner's words for this world were "dark and futuristic", "slow appearing animations, motion graphics, transitions and hover effects", "clean cool", and nothing that reads as a generated template.
keyCharacteristics: One carbon ground, one bone ink, and two voices as light: ember (you) and frost (them).
Hairline rules instead of boxes; corners of 2px and 3px; no pills.
Wide, light Roboto Flex for the instrument's own words; Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for everything read at a glance.
Your side on the left, theirs mirrored on the right, the measurements between them.
Outlines that fill from their own side under the pointer; quiet actions that draw a line.
Slow arrivals on an exponential ease-out; nothing overshoots; reduced motion means still.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Ember is you and frost is them, everywhere the two appear, and they are always paired with a text label ("You speak", "Them"), never colour alone. No other element may borrow either hue.

rules.name: The Bone Accent Rule
rules.body: Links, focus rings, switches and the ordinary primary button are bone. Colour stays with the voices and the states.

rules.name: The Light Without Glow Rule
rules.body: A voice is a line, a letter or a flat fill. It never blurs, blooms or casts coloured light. The lamp's pulse is a 1px ring that leaves it, and the pipeline's light is a segment travelling along a 1px line.

rules.name: The Tested Contrast Scope
rules.body: `contrast.test.ts` reads the hex `light-dark()` tokens from `base.css` and checks, in both themes, exactly three things: `--text-faint` at 4.5:1 or better on `--bg`, `--surface` and `--surface-2`; `--control-border` at 3:1 or better on the same three; and `--ok`, `--warn`, `--danger` and `--accent` at 4.5:1 or better on their own `-soft` ground. The voices, `--text-muted`, `--surface-3`, `--on-channel`, the hairlines and dimmed states are not covered by it; a change to those needs its own check.

rules.name: The Measurement Rule
rules.body: Martian Mono is only for measurements and code: clock times, delays, counts, slider values, provider ids, `kbd`. It never sets a name, a label or a sentence.

rules.name: The Wide Capitals Rule
rules.body: A name of a thing (a speaker, a language, a pipeline step, a service, a measurement's title, a key, a control, a tab) is Roboto Flex in capitals, at 9px to 13px, width 132% or wider, with positive tracking. These are the labels of parts on an instrument; they are not kickers above headings.

rules.name: The Captions First Rule
rules.body: Anything read at a glance during a call is Atkinson Hyperlegible, and the translation is the heaviest and largest text in the conversation. Decoration never competes with it.

rules.name: The Nastaliq Room Rule
rules.body: Urdu gets its own line-height and its own face; anything pinned over scrolling Urdu fades the text out beneath it over a full caption line (34px to 40px) instead of slicing its deep strokes, and the masks a rising Urdu line travels behind are opened by 0.55em so no stroke is cut.

rules.name: The One Edge Rule
rules.body: The masthead, both units and the conversation start on the same left edge, 24px, or 14px at 860px and below.

rules.name: The Mirror Rule
rules.body: Whatever your side does from the left, their side does from the right: alignment, row direction, the pipeline's direction, the meter, and the side a key fills from.

rules.name: The Drawn, Never Boxed Rule
rules.body: The page's structure is ruled with 1px hairlines between bands, rows and columns. Outlines belong to controls and to layers that float (dialogs, popovers, menus); a section of the page is never put in a box. A line set across all columns breaks their rules; a rule must never strike through text.

rules.name: The Flat Dark Rule
rules.body: Nothing on the page itself casts a shadow. A shadow means the thing floats above the page and will go away again.

rules.name: The Own Side Rule
rules.body: A fill enters from the side the control belongs to: buttons from the left, your key from the left, their key from the right. A filled control empties under the pointer when its action is to undo itself.

rules.name: The Slow Arrival Rule
rules.body: Things arrive on `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`: quick to answer, long to settle, never overshooting. Arrivals on the page take 0.6s to 2.2s (small changes inside dialogs and notices, such as a tab panel, a banner or a toast, take 0.24s to 0.36s); the page's own opening runs about three seconds, but the keys are there first and at once, because starting a channel must never wait. Things fade in where they stand: the one movement of the opening is the two direction titles coming into focus (30px, 10px blur, 2.2s), and blur exists only there and on the sentences already present when the page opens. Leaving is quicker than arriving (a dialog 0.24s, the empty page 0.3s). Presses answer in 0.12s. Motion only ever shows what the state already says; it never delays audio, the network or the transcript.

rules.name: The Step Back Rule
rules.body: Hover focus in the conversation dims the words of the other rows or columns (the caption cells) to opacity 0.78 over 0.6s, no further; the speaker, the time and the delay are not dimmed, and a language tag inside a caption goes to muted bone. It applies only while the pointer is in use (the component clears the state 2.6s after the pointer rests, and it applies only where hover exists). A pointer parked on the conversation never dims a call.

rules.name: The Still Rule
rules.body: With `prefers-reduced-motion`, transitions and animations collapse to nothing, GSAP timelines and smooth scrolling do not start, and the surface is a single frame.

dos: Do keep ember for your voice and frost for theirs in every new element that belongs to a side, with a text label beside the colour.
Do draw structure with 1px `hairline` / `hairline-strong` rules and keep corners at 2px (3px for floating layers).
Do set names of things in Roboto Flex wide capitals (width 132% or more, positive tracking, 9px to 13px) and titles wide and light (weight 280 to 330).
Do set every number that is measured (a time, a delay, a count, a slider value) and every identifier in Martian Mono with tabular figures.
Do mirror anything added to one side of the console on the other.
Do let outlined controls fill from their own side over 0.55s to 0.7s on `--ease-out`, and let quiet actions draw a 1px line.
Do define any new colour once as a `light-dark()` pair and check it in both themes; extend `contrast.test.ts` when the pair carries text or a control edge.
Do give every new motion a reduced-motion answer, and keep it off the capture path and independent of timers.
Do bundle every asset; nothing is fetched at run time.
donts: Don't bring back the neon "AI studio": purple glows, gradient ribbons, glass or backdrop blur. The owner asked for nothing that reads as generated effects.
Don't bring back the pale editorial page as the default; the owner rejected it, and light exists only as the Daylight variant of these same tokens.
Don't make a voice glow, bloom or blur. Gradients here are tools (a sweep fill, a travelling light on a line, a fade under a pinned head, the stroke of the surface), never decoration.
Don't use pills or large radii; the only round things are points of state.
Don't box a section of the page; outlines are for controls and floating layers.
Don't use ember or frost for anything that is not one of the two voices, and don't use a state colour for decoration.
Don't set names, labels or sentences in Martian Mono.
Don't add bounce, overshoot or elastic easing, and don't make the keys wait for an entrance.
Don't dim unfocused captions below opacity 0.78, and don't dim at all without a moving pointer.
Don't let a notice, a popover or an animation cover or delay a caption.
